spec.title: Pin the in-flight ceiling with a boundary pair computed from the constant
spec.problem: gate-phase-entry.mjs's `inFlight()` decides whether the phase-entry guard evaluates a record AT ALL: outside the window it abstains from every rule, so every other assertion in test-gate-phase-entry.sh only runs for a record inside it. The window is `IN_FLIGHT_MS`, module-private at HEAD, and nothing asserts either side of its boundary. The suite's only two fixture ages (1h and 25h, test-gate-phase-entry.sh:38-39) are the only thing holding it, so the constant is free to move almost a full day in either direction with every gate suite green. Re-measured in this worktree at HEAD (5dd6a9e, after #61's +192 lines), the green window is (1.0h, 25.05h) on a 24h constant, and the value 2h -- which would make the guard refuse to evaluate any run left alone over a long lunch -- is fully green at 558/0. WHAT THIS CHANGE DOES NOT DO, stated here because the sentence above invites the opposite reading: #63 pins the predicate's RELATIONSHIP to the constant, not the constant's admissible RANGE. AC5 REQUIRES that a value rewrite keep the new pair green, so after #63 the value 2h is STILL fully green and the value's green window is unchanged at approximately (1.0h, 25.05h), bounded solely by AC11's two premise assertions. Narrowing that range is a retune, and a retune is q3, deliberately not answered here. Separately, the map found the same number spelled out FIVE more times outside its owner -- the count in measured_state, which is the authoritative one -- including once inside this very suite's own fixture-qualification probe. Two of those five are Lane 1's and are fixed here (R7); the other three are routed to #74. The guard's two false claims of SHARED DEFINITION are a separate defect and are NOT part of that count: they are prose, not spellings of the number, and R2/AC12 fix both sites here.
spec.root_cause: `IN_FLIGHT_MS` is module-private, so no test can compute a fixture age from it. Every existing age is therefore a fixed literal that happens to straddle the boundary rather than a value derived from it, which is the same class as #33: a threshold pinned by whatever the population happened to be, decaying silently as soon as either side moves.
requirements: R1. Export `IN_FLIGHT_MS` from plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs. The literal value (`24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`), `inFlight()`, and every call site stay byte-identical; the only change to the module's behaviour is that the symbol becomes readable from outside. Do NOT export `inFlight` itself -- see ba_notes for why. The module shape properties the declared expected survivor RESTS ON are preserved and asserted (AC13), with the honest scope AC13 now states: `Date.now()` continues to occur exactly once in the module (:664, verified at HEAD); the initializer that feeds `inFlight` continues to be spelled exactly `  const now = Date.now();` (`grep -c '^  const now = Date\.now();$'` returns 1 at HEAD, verified in this worktree); and the module continues to export no `inFlight`, asserted by dynamic import rather than by grep. Those three catch the CHEAP ways the survivor's justification stops holding. THEY DO NOT CLOSE THE CLASS, and R1 no longer claims they do: SecOps measured that an override threaded into `inFlight`'s `now` ARGUMENT at the call site (:538) leaves all three green while making the guard's clock millisecond-exact from outside. That residual is recorded in expected_survivor as a REVIEW OBLIGATION on any future edit to `inFlight`'s `now` argument, not as a mechanized guarantee.

R2. Correct the guard's claim of shared definition with pipeline-status.mjs at BOTH sites, not only the header. Site one is gate-phase-entry.mjs:26-27 ('reusing pipeline-status.mjs's own 24h / no-final-verdict definition rather than inventing a second one'), which is flatly false: there is no shared symbol and both modules hold their own literal. Site two is gate-phase-entry.mjs:490-491, in `inFlight`'s own doc comment ('the predicate pipeline-status.mjs already uses to call a run "possibly stuck", inverted'), which is TRUE today and becomes FALSE silently the moment either literal moves -- which is the exact drift risk R2 exists to name. State the duplication as a live, unresolved drift risk, cite issue #74, and site the drift-risk sentence AT `inFlight` where the predicate is, not only in the file header 465 lines above it. THE SITING IS MECHANIZED (AC12 iii): the replacement must name `#74` on a line inside the 20 lines ABOVE the line matching `^function inFlight(` -- :495 at HEAD, so the band is :475-:494 and the corrected doc comment at :489-:494 sits inside it. Reason, demonstrated by SecOps: AC12's two zero-hit greps are satisfied by DELETING the :490-491 clause outright, which leaves no drift-risk sentence anywhere near the predicate and nothing citing #74 anywhere in the file. Change nothing in pipeline-status.mjs.

R3. Add a MILLISECOND-grained fixture-age helper to test-gate-phase-entry.sh alongside the existing `iso_hours_ago`, and read `IN_FLIGHT_MS` out of the module once, at suite start, via the already-exercised dynamic-import path (`node --input-type=module -e 'const m = await import(...)'`, the mechanism `probe43` uses at :983). Hour granularity cannot express a margin small enough to sit inside the window without rounding. MARGIN IS PINNED HERE, because everything downstream assumed a number the spec never wrote down: MARGIN = 300000 ms (5 minutes), by q1's two-sided rule -- at least two orders of magnitude above the measured fixture-write-to-gate-return elapsed (DBA measured 237 / 227 / 239 ms over three runs on one machine, so 300000 ms carries roughly 1250x headroom) and under 1% of the window (0.35% at 24h). Note the grain: that elapsed is fixture-write-to-gate-RETURN, which is NOT DevOps' 80-90 ms figure for a bare CLI invocation; the two measure different spans and must not be averaged or substituted for each other. THE READ MUST BE ASSERTED, not merely performed -- and the assertion is NOT 'a positive integer of plausible magnitude', which is exactly one adjective short of the precondition the fixtures actually need. Assert `Number.isFinite`, integer, AND `IN_FLIGHT_MS > 2 * MARGIN`, and say why in the assertion message: any positive value at or below MARGIN makes the INSIDE age `IN_FLIGHT_MS - MARGIN` zero or NEGATIVE, i.e. dates the fixture in the FUTURE, and DBA verified against the real CLI that a `3-impl`/architectural record dated five minutes in the future yields `refused` rc 2 -- the guard has no floor (gate-phase-entry.mjs:499; the missing clamp is deferred to #74 section 5, and this is where that deferral has a live consequence INSIDE #63). The INSIDE cell would then PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON while only the OUTSIDE cell reddened: the 'detection by luck' this requirement exists to prevent, surviving the requirement's own assertion. MEASURED REASON, CORRECTED -- round 1's justification was half false in the flattering direction, and an implementer would have gone looking at the wrong failure. Under harness.sh:5's `set -u`, /bin/bash 3.2.57 does NOT silently swallow every bad read: `IN_FLIGHT_MS=""; $(( IN_FLIGHT_MS - MARGIN ))` yields -300000 with rc 0 and no diagnostic (SILENT -- this is the real shell hazard), while `IN_FLIGHT_MS="undefined"` ABORTS LOUDLY ('undefined: unbound variable', rc 1) because arithmetic expansion resolves the bare word as a variable NAME; `NaN` and node error text abort the same way, and `1e3` aborts with 'value too great for base'. So the silent SHELL case is the EMPTY read, and the silent JS case is `undefined` at probe43 (`age > undefined` is false). Two different sites, two different mechanisms; the requirement stands on both.

R4. Add the boundary PAIR, both cells driven through the real CLI with the existing `gate()` helper, both at a guarded phase with an absent prerequisite (`3-impl` at the architectural tier, matching the existing AC15(a)/(b) cells): INSIDE, `updated_at` = now minus (IN_FLIGHT_MS - MARGIN), the guard evaluates and REFUSES; OUTSIDE, `updated_at` = now minus (IN_FLIGHT_MS + MARGIN), the guard abstains with the not-in-flight reason. Both ages COMPUTED from the value read in R3; no hour or millisecond literal on either line.

R5. Assert, do not print, that the wall-clock elapsed between writing the INSIDE fixture and the gate returning is below MARGIN. The INSIDE cell is the only elapsed-sensitive one (its effective age is IN_FLIGHT_MS - MARGIN + elapsed), and an unasserted margin turns a slow runner into a flake rather than a failure.

R6. Add the non-zero control the issue requires: drive the IDENTICAL two fixtures with the IDENTICAL driver against a SHIFTED-boundary copy of the guard placed outside the checkout (a harness `new_tmpdir`), and require the INSIDE cell to flip to `not-applicable` while the OUTSIDE cell holds at `not-applicable`, both as real decisions on stdout. The control must DISCRIMINATE, not merely fire: a copy that is simply broken fails open to silence, which is not `not-applicable`. THREE MECHANICS ARE MANDATORY, not advisory, AND (a) AND (b) BIND EVERY OFF-CHECKOUT GUARD COPY IN THIS SPEC -- AC7's shifted-boundary control AND AC14's no-export driver -- not AC7 alone. That scoping IS the round-2 blocker: AC10's exercised half inherited neither mandate and went green over exactly the unvalidated probe it was written to reject. (a) Copy the WHOLE `plugins/pipeline/scripts/` directory into the tmpdir, never gate-phase-entry.mjs alone: the guard imports ./lib.mjs, ./dispatch-model.mjs, ./pipeline-telemetry.mjs and ./validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs by relative path, and a one-file copy throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND straight into the guard's own fail-open-on-tooling-error catch, producing exactly the silent exit-0 no-decision that AC7 says must not be mistaken for a real `not-applicable`. DBA prototyped this over 6 whole-directory copies and 212+ CLI invocations with zero import failures, and confirmed `broken -> <SILENT> rc=1` is distinguishable from `not-applicable rc=0`. (b) EVERY cell driven against such a copy asserts on the STRING the run produced -- the DECISION string (`GATE_DEC`, which the existing `gate()` helper already falls back to `<no-decision-on-stdout>` for) for the boundary cells, and the EXACT diagnosis sentence for AC14's probe cells -- never on the exit code alone and NEVER on `!= "ok"`. MEASURED: probe43 folds stderr into stdout (`2>&1`, test-gate-phase-entry.sh:1012), so against a one-file copy an `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` stack trace satisfies `!= "ok"` IDENTICALLY for the validated and the unvalidated probe. DBA's 2x2 (validated/unvalidated probe x export/no-export guard, whole-dir copies, 437.84h fixture) shows the underlying validation works -- 'past the ceiling' / 'did not read as a finite positive number' / 'past the ceiling' / 'ok' -- so only the driver and the assertion were ever wrong. (c) AC7's boundary SHIFT MUST BE VALUE-RELATIVE, never a rewrite of the literal `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`: locate the declaration by `^export const IN_FLIGHT_MS = .*;$`, assert EXACTLY ONE matching line, and write a value COMPUTED from the value read in R3 that is strictly below the INSIDE fixture's age -- `floor((IN_FLIGHT_MS - MARGIN) / 2)` works at every base value. Reason, measured: under AC5's 48h rewrite the 24h literal occurs ZERO times in the build the suite is running against, so a literal-shift control dies or reddens there and becomes a THIRD red cell that falsifies AC5 axis 3's declaration for a reason unrelated to the constant.

R7. Replace the two hardcoded re-derivations of the ceiling inside this suite -- the capture tripwire at test-gate-phase-entry.sh:612 and `probe43`'s staleness diagnosis at :999 -- with reads of the exported constant. Both currently spell `24 * 3600e3` while judging fixtures against a ceiling they do not own. THREE CONSTRAINTS ON THE SUBSTITUTION. (a) EACH SITE MUST VALIDATE WHAT IT READ before comparing against it, because the substituted value can arrive as `undefined` where a literal could not, and `age > undefined` and `age > NaN` are both FALSE. Measured with the real 437.84h-old capture: with the literal, `age > 24*3600e3` is true and the site diagnoses staleness; with `undefined` or `NaN` the comparison is false and the site returns 'ok', diagnosing nothing -- a check that CLAIMS MORE than it knows, silently, about the ~345 assertions `probe43` qualifies fixtures for. Require an explicit guard at each site pushing ONE EXACT SENTENCE, the same at both: `if (!Number.isFinite(CEIL) || CEIL <= 0) bad.push("the exported IN_FLIGHT_MS did not read as a finite positive number");`. AC14 exercises it, on a driver that can tell a validated probe from an unvalidated one. This is also the DOWN-PATH answer: a partial revert of #63 that removes the export but keeps R7's reads silently vacates probe43's staleness branch, and without this guard nothing else in AC1-AC14 notices. (b) PRESERVE THE EXACT COMPARISON at :999. probe43 spells 'past the ceiling' as `age > CEIL`, the exact complement of the guard's `now - updated <= IN_FLIGHT_MS`. Substituting the constant must not turn `>` into `>=`. R7(b) NOW HAS A CHECK, which it did not in round 1: AC14(c) makes the branch LIVE (DBA measured that at HEAD both `>` -> `>=` and DELETING the whole staleness push leave the suite at 462/0, because all three call sites assert `== "ok"` and no fixture is past the ceiling -- so the substitution would have moved a dead literal to a dead read). The `>`-vs-`>=` distinction ITSELF stays unpinned and is declared a SECOND EXPECTED SURVIVOR, for the same reason as the guard's `<=`-vs-`<` 500 lines away: it is the exact complement of that distinction and no CLI-driven fixture lands on the exact millisecond. (c) THE DIAGNOSIS MUST STOP SPELLING THE NUMBER, and no existing assertion LABEL may be renamed. probe43's message reads 'updated_at is past the 24h ceiling'; a message that says 24h while comparing against a constant that may not be 24h is the same false claim in prose that R2 corrects in the guard's header. Reword it to name the ceiling without its value (e.g. 'updated_at is past the in-flight ceiling: this cell would test staleness'), and reword the SECOND prose site the same way: :39's fixture comment reads `# past R6's 24h ceiling`, which is the identical false-when-it-moves claim about the identical ceiling (`grep -c '24h ceiling'` returns 2 at HEAD, measured). :39 is a COMMENT edit only -- the 25h literal stays, per out_of_scope. That string is a runtime diagnosis, not an assertion label, so AC2's containment is unaffected -- whereas :611's LABEL ('the capture is still permanently stale (>24h), which is what (c) tests') must stay byte-identical, since renaming it breaks AC2 for a reason that has nothing to do with this change.

R8. Assert the PREMISES of the two existing fixture ages against the exported constant: FRESH_ISO's age is inside the window and STALE_ISO's age is outside it. These two assertions carry more weight than their own cells and the spec says so deliberately, so that a later author does not delete them as a nicety. (a) The two ages are load-bearing for 400-plus assertions and their in/out status is assumed today, never stated. (b) The INSIDE premise is the only thing standing between AC24 (test-gate-phase-entry.sh:891, the suite's only assertion over the production-row corpus) and a VACUOUS green: AC24 rewrites every committed record's `updated_at` to FRESH_ISO precisely so staleness cannot mask the table, and its pass set is `granted|not-applicable`, so if FRESH_ISO ever fell outside the window every corpus record would abstain, AC24's zero would stay green over a wholly abstaining population, and its accounting assertion would pass too. (c) The two premises are, after this change, the ONLY remaining bound on the VALUE of IN_FLIGHT_MS -- everything else in the suite becomes derived and therefore value-independent -- and their assertion messages must say so. (d) EXPECTED READING OF THE R8(b) CONTROL, so a run that comes out differently is legible: DBA drove `FRESH_ISO="$(iso_hours_ago 1)"` -> `iso_hours_ago 30` and measured the entry suite at 228 passed / 234 failed with BOTH AC24 cells GREEN (`#43-C1 the walk ACCOUNTS for every committed record` and `no committed record is refused by the table`). AC11's inside premise is therefore the only DIAGNOSIS of that state, not the only DETECTION -- 234 other assertions redden in the same run. Do not read AC11 as the sole signal.

R9. Register every new assertion under the existing id ledger and its two meta-tests (the `#61-Z1`/`#61-Z2` uniqueness-and-registration pattern at the bottom of the file), and pin the new work by LABEL SET, never by an assertion-count floor (#33). EVERY NEW LABEL CARRIES THE `#63-` PREFIX, which the file's own comment blocks at :933 and :1422 establish as the fix for exactly this hazard, and which is why #43's and #61's cells carry `#43-` and `#61-`. Measured reason: `grep -n 'AC11' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh` returns SIX lines over THREE unrelated subjects (:527 and :541, the tier-row family; :933 and :1154, comments; :1803 and :1805, #61's own AC11), so a spec-criterion number is not a name a grep can resolve -- and AC5 rests a load-bearing expected-red DECLARATION on one. TWO IDS ARE PINNED BY THIS SPEC because other criteria name them: `#63-P1` is FRESH_ISO's inside premise and `#63-P2` is STALE_ISO's outside premise (AC11). The remaining new cells choose their own suffixes under the same prefix.

R10. #37 compliance: no new population is derived from a range against a moving ref. The boundary pair's population is two constructed fixtures in a `new_tmpdir`, and the control's population is those same two. Any before/after comparison of the suite's label set (AC2) is a Phase 4 REVIEW step, not an in-suite assertion, precisely so nothing in the tree ever resolves `<remote>/main..HEAD`.
acceptance_criteria: AC1. `grep -c '^export const IN_FLIGHT_MS' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs` returns 1, and the declaration's value is still exactly `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`. BOTH HALVES RESOLVE THE CHECKOUT PATH -- `$REPO_ROOT/plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`, and test-gate-phase-entry.sh:29 already derives REPO_ROOT from PLUGIN_ROOT, which no SCRIPTS_DIR redirect moves -- and NEVER `$GUARD`/`$SCRIPTS_DIR`. Reason: AC5 runs this same suite against a REWRITTEN copy in which the value half is false by construction, so a $GUARD-bound assertion reddens at 48h with the checkout untouched and becomes a third red cell. If REPO_ROOT resolves empty the cell FAILS with that as its message; it does not skip.

AC2. All three gate suites pass, and the LABEL SET of each (test-gate-phase-entry.sh, -drift.sh, -hook.sh) is a superset of its label set at the base commit -- set containment, not a count. Verified in Phase 4 by capturing both label sets and diffing them; not asserted inside the suite (see R10). test-gate-phase-entry-hook.sh is a Lane 3 file and must pass wholly unmodified. LABEL INVARIANCE, because R7 edits two existing sites: the substitution may not RENAME any existing assertion label. Specifically :611's `the capture is still permanently stale (>24h), which is what (c) tests` stays byte-identical -- it is prose about a 437.84h capture that is stale under any window this spec admits, and renaming it breaks containment for a reason unrelated to the change. probe43's internal diagnosis strings are NOT labels, and R7(c) deliberately changes one.

AC3. INSIDE cell: a `3-impl`/architectural record with no prerequisite artifact and no events, `updated_at` = now - (IN_FLIGHT_MS - MARGIN), driven through `node gate-phase-entry.mjs --root <root>`, yields decision `refused` and exit code 2.
AC4. OUTSIDE cell: the same record body with `updated_at` = now - (IN_FLIGHT_MS + MARGIN) yields decision `not-applicable`, exit code 0, and a reason containing `is not in flight`.

AC5. DRIFT IMMUNITY, SCOPED TO THE PAIR AND TO ONE SUITE. Both boundary fixture ages are computed at run time from the module's exported value, so rewriting the constant in a scratch copy moves both ages with it and THE TWO BOUNDARY CELLS STAY GREEN -- verified in BOTH directions, a rewrite well below 24h (2h) and well above it (48h), because a single hardcoded age survives a rewrite in one direction and not the other. MECHANISM, which exists and needs no edit to the checkout: harness.sh:11 is `SCRIPTS_DIR="${SCRIPTS_DIR:-...}"`, so `SCRIPTS_DIR=<tmpdir-copy-of-the-whole-scripts-dir> /bin/bash plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh` drives a rewritten build with the checkout untouched (AC8 holds). THE CLAIM IS ABOUT THE PAIR, AND THE EXPECTED-RED DECLARATION IS SCOPED TO test-gate-phase-entry.sh ONLY. Under the 48h copy, in THAT suite, EXACTLY TWO cells are expected red, each named by something a grep resolves: (i) the existing label `(a) 25h old, no final verdict -> not-applicable even at a guarded phase` at :602 (`grep -c '(a) 25h old'` returns 1, so the name is unique), and (ii) `#63-P2`, AC11's OUTSIDE premise (R9 pins that id). Both fail for the same correct reason -- STALE_ISO is a 25h LITERAL and 25h is legitimately INSIDE a 48h window. Neither is evidence against AC5. The two admissible responses are to leave the red or to record it; rebasing STALE_ISO onto the constant is forbidden by out_of_scope and deleting AC11's premise is forbidden by R8(b). NEVER NAME AN EXPECTED-RED CELL BY SPEC-CRITERION NUMBER: `grep -n 'AC11' test-gate-phase-entry.sh` returns six lines over three unrelated subjects (R9). THE SCOPE SENTENCE IS LOAD-BEARING, because the mechanism is NOT transparent and a whole-set reader would otherwise count three reds and conclude the declaration is wrong. MEASURED, twice, in two environments: an UNMODIFIED whole-directory copy under SCRIPTS_DIR leaves test-gate-phase-entry.sh at 462/0 but takes test-gate-phase-entry-hook.sh from 59/0 to 57/2, at EVERY value (24h, 2h, 48h alike). The two reds are :396 `test-voice-lint.sh still passes exactly its 48 assertions (41 pre-existing + 7 from #27)` and its `with none failing` companion at :397, because test-voice-lint.sh itself measures 44/4 when SCRIPTS_DIR is redirected. That is an artefact of the REDIRECTION, not of the constant. So the expected reading of a whole-set run at 48h is THREE reds, not two: entry suite = exactly the two cells named above and no others, hook suite = 57/2 (the artefact, present at every value), drift suite = 37/0 (it does not read the window). At 24h and at 2h the entry suite is 462/0 and both named cells are GREEN, so the declaration DISCRIMINATES rather than merely permits.

AC6. The INSIDE cell carries an ASSERTION (not a printf, not a comment) that the measured wall-clock between fixture write and gate return is strictly less than MARGIN, which is 300000 ms and is pinned in R3 rather than left to the implementer.

AC7. NON-ZERO CONTROL, DISCRIMINATING, WITH A VALUE-RELATIVE SHIFT. Against a shifted-boundary copy of the WHOLE scripts directory located outside the checkout, the INSIDE fixture flips from `refused` to `not-applicable` while the OUTSIDE fixture stays `not-applicable`, and BOTH runs are asserted on the DECISION STRING read from stdout -- not on the exit code -- so that the silent fail-open (`<no-decision-on-stdout>`, which an rc-only assertion reads as a pass) is separable from a real `not-applicable`. A one-file copy of the guard produces exactly that silent case via MODULE_NOT_FOUND into the guard's fail-open catch; the criterion is not satisfied by a control that cannot tell the two apart. THE SHIFT IS COMPUTED, NEVER SPELLED (R6c): the control locates the declaration by `^export const IN_FLIGHT_MS = .*;$`, asserts exactly one matching line, and writes `floor((IN_FLIGHT_MS - MARGIN) / 2)` from the value read at suite start -- so the control still works when the base it copies has itself been rewritten. Measured reason: in AC5's 48h build the literal `const IN_FLIGHT_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;` occurs ZERO times, so a literal-rewrite control dies or reddens there and manufactures a third red cell that falsifies AC5's declaration for an unrelated reason.
AC8. `git status --porcelain` inside the plugin tree is empty after the suite has run. The control never edits a tracked file, so an interrupted run cannot leave a shifted constant in the checkout.

AC9. PREDICATE MUTATIONS REDDEN THE PAIR. Two mutations to `inFlight`, applied one at a time to a scratch copy, each redden at least one of the two cells: (i) `now - updated <= IN_FLIGHT_MS` becomes `now - updated >= IN_FLIGHT_MS`; (ii) the age term is deleted so the predicate returns true whenever there is no final verdict. This is the criterion that shows the pair reads the constant rather than merely equalling itself. NOTE: mutating the constant's VALUE must NOT redden the pair -- by AC5 that is the point -- so the value mutation is not admissible evidence here.

AC10. THE TWO RE-DERIVED CEILINGS ARE GONE, AND SO IS THE NUMBER IN THE PROSE BESIDE THEM. `grep -n '24 *\* *3600e3' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh` returns zero hits; both former sites (:612 capture tripwire, :999 probe43) read the exported constant; the capture tripwire still reports `stale` for `exp-script-test-coverage` as captured; and `grep -c '24h ceiling' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh` returns 0, because no prose in this suite may keep asserting '24h' about a ceiling it now reads from a constant that may not be 24h (R7c). NON-ZERO CONTROL AND SCOPE, both measured in this worktree at HEAD: that grep returns 2 today, and the two hits are :999 (probe43's diagnosis) AND :39 (`STALE_ISO="$(iso_hours_ago 25)"    # past R6's 24h ceiling`), so BOTH must be reworded. :39's is a comment-only edit -- the 25h literal itself stays, per out_of_scope. THE GREP IS ON THE PHRASE `24h ceiling`, NOT ON `24h`, deliberately: `grep -c '24h'` returns 3 at HEAD and the third hit is :611's assertion LABEL, which AC2 requires to stay byte-identical. A zero-hit rule over the bare number would put this criterion in direct conflict with AC2. The two former sites are mutated SEPARATELY in the falsifiability pass, since restoring one and restoring both are indistinguishable to a zero-hit grep and that hides a dead site. THE VALIDATION AND LIVENESS HALVES ARE NOW AC14, split out of this criterion in round 2: a grep-shaped check and an exercised check have different failure modes, and folding them left the exercised half inheriting none of R6's mechanics and passing identically over a validated and an unvalidated probe.

AC11. Two premise assertions, computed from the exported constant and labelled `#63-P1` (FRESH_ISO's age is strictly less than IN_FLIGHT_MS) and `#63-P2` (STALE_ISO's age is strictly greater than IN_FLIGHT_MS); AC5 names `#63-P2` in its expected-red set, so the ids are normative (R9). Their assertion MESSAGES must state what they are for, because both facts are invisible from the cells themselves: the INSIDE premise is what keeps AC24's corpus zero from going vacuous over a wholly abstaining population (R8b), and the two together are the ONLY remaining bound on the VALUE of IN_FLIGHT_MS after this change -- approximately (1.0h, 25.05h) -- since every other new assertion is derived and therefore value-independent.

AC12. BOTH shared-definition claims are corrected, the corrections are SITED, and each check has its own control. (i) `git grep -n 'reusing pipeline-status' plugins/pipeline/scripts/` returns zero hits (non-zero control confirmed: exactly 1 hit at HEAD). (ii) `git grep -n 'already uses to call a run' plugins/pipeline/scripts/` returns zero hits (non-zero control: exactly 1 hit at HEAD, gate-phase-entry.mjs:491). SecOps demonstrated the hole it closes: deleting the :490-491 clause outright, with no replacement text at all, passes (i) and (ii) while leaving no drift-risk sentence anywhere near `inFlight` and nothing citing #74 in the file. WHAT IS NOT MECHANIZED, stated rather than implied: the CONTENT of the replacement sentence -- that pipeline-status.mjs:156 holds an independent copy of the same number with no shared symbol -- is a Phase 4 human read. AC13. THE SURVIVOR'S PREMISE IS PINNED WHERE IT LANDED, AND THE PIN IS NARROWER THAN THE PROPERTY. Three assertions over gate-phase-entry.mjs, all resolving the CHECKOUT path (AC1's rule): (a) `Date.now()` appears exactly once in the module (at :664 today); (b) the INITIALIZER that feeds `inFlight` is spelled exactly `  const now = Date.now();` -- `grep -c '^  const now = Date\.now();$'` returns 1, verified 1 at HEAD; (c) the module exports no `inFlight`, asserted by DYNAMIC IMPORT (`typeof m.inFlight === 'undefined'`) and NOT by grep, because SecOps demonstrated that appending `export { inFlight };` leaves `grep -c '^export function inFlight'` at 0 while the import reads `function`. WHAT THESE CATCH AND WHAT THEY DO NOT, measured by SecOps over six mutations, stated here because the round-1 wording claimed more than it held: (b) catches an env or flag override folded into the single read (`const now = Number(process.env.GATE_NOW) || Date.now();`), which (a) MISSES because the token count stays exactly 1; (a) catches the clock re-spelled as `new Date().getTime()`; (c) catches an added export. resolution.answer: Leave it at 24h and do not retune in this diff. THE DIRECTION ARGUMENT, CORRECTED -- the earlier wording ('the failure direction is toward ABSTENTION, so nothing is shipping a falsehood') was one-sided and a later reader would have inherited it as an unqualified principle. It holds for the LOW side only. A NARROWER window makes the guard abstain where it should refuse: that is a silence, and SecOps' vulnerability note shows the silence is total, since stop.sh discards the decision line. A WIDER window makes the guard REFUSE turns it should not: the guard's own header (:26-27) says the ceiling exists precisely because the Stop hook is PROJECT-scoped, so without it an abandoned run parked at a guarded phase would refuse every turn in that project forever -- and the mtime fallback picks the newest status.json in the project, which the session may not even own. That is an availability cost, not a silence. In the currently measured window the asymmetry favours the ruling by a wide margin: the upside is +4.4% (about +63 minutes of additional project-scoped turn-blocking before anything reddens) against a downside of -95.6% (the constant can fall to 1/23rd of its value). So: the low side is silence, the high side is availability, bounded here at roughly +1.05h of extra project-scoped blocking. Leaving the value alone stands, and the right time to answer the question is after the boundary is pinned rather than while it is not. Recorded so Phase 4 can check the build did not quietly change the value.

concerns.description: AC7's non-zero control requires a 'shifted-boundary copy of the guard placed outside the checkout' that must DISCRIMINATE (INSIDE flips to not-applicable, OUTSIDE stays not-applicable, both print a real decision on stdout) rather than merely fail open to silence. I read gate-phase-entry.mjs's imports directly: it pulls from four sibling files by relative path -- `./lib.mjs`, `./dispatch-model.mjs`, `./pipeline-telemetry.mjs`, `./validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs`. This is the same failure class the guard's own gate() test helper already guards against (`GATE_DEC` falls back to `<no-decision-on-stdout>` when stdout has no decision field), so the suite CAN catch a broken copy if the boundary-pair cells assert on GATE_DEC's literal value rather than just exit code -- but only if Dev copies (or symlinks) all four sibling modules alongside the shifted gate-phase-entry.mjs into the new_tmpdir, not just the one file. Not a spec defect (R4/R6 already route the pair through the real CLI via the existing gate() helper, which is the right call), but worth stating explicitly for Dev since getting the copy step wrong makes AC7 pass for the wrong reason -- a broken copy and a correctly shifted copy can both read as 'not-applicable' unless the reason string is checked too.

rulings.item: 6. THE RULING ASKED FOR: is the content half mechanizable?
rulings.question: #63-H1/H2/H3 pin the drift note's REMOVAL and LOCATION, never its CONTENT, and that sentence has now shipped false FOUR times, green every time. Dev rewrote the PR body's known-limits section to say so in those terms. Is that the right resolution, or is the content half mechanizable and owed a follow-up?
rulings.ruling: THE PROSE REWRITE IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, AND IT IS NOT THE RIGHT RESOLUTION ON ITS OWN. The content half IS mechanizable. I know because I built most of it during this review, in one sitting, with a firing non-zero control -- and it caught QA-D2, which 493 cells did not. Naming an unpinned sentence in the known-limits section is honest, and strictly better than the abstract caveat it replaces, but honesty about an unpinned claim is not a substitute for pinning it. The empirical record decides this: the round that rewrote the PR body to say `the tests pin removal and location, never content` is the SAME round that shipped a new content falsehood into that very docblock. The failure rate of the prose-only approach is 4 for 4. `Do not try a fourth time` is refuted by demonstration -- so I will not say it, because I would be wrong.
rulings.why_the_previous_three_attempts_failed: They tried to pin the SENTENCE. That is unbuildable: a comment is not an interface, any assertion over its text is a restatement that tracks whoever last edited it, and it breaks on every legitimate rewording. The buildable target is not the prose. It is the PROPOSITION the prose asserts, checked against the live modules the prose is about. #63-H1/H2/H3 correctly stopped at removal and location because they were aiming at the wrong object.
